newsitem.title: UK: Man sees world 96/97 sugar output at 123.5 mln t.
newsitem.headline: Man sees world 96/97 sugar output at 123.5 mln t.

text.p: World production of sugar should rise to 123.54 million tonnes raw value in the 1996/97 crop year from 123.48 million tonnes a year ago, international trade house E D & F Man said in a report released on Thursday.

In its first estimate of the global 1996/97 balance, Man said there would be another year of surplus in world markets and pegged the balance at 3.62 million tonnes, which equated to 4.3 million tonnes on an October/September basis.
The sugar surplus last season was 5.66 million tonnes, though much of this quantity had been added to stocks, primarily in India, Man said.
Sugar production in the European Union (EU) was forecast to fall by 331,000 tonnes to 16.67 million tonnes, with the largest decline in leading producer France.
While world sugar production was forecast only marginally higher then in 1995/96, consumption was estimated to increase by two million tonnes to 119.91 million tonnes, Man said.

The beet sector would continue to surrender its share of global production to cane and, at 36.07 million tonnes, account for under 30 percent of the total output. Beet production reached 36.43 million tonnes in 1995/96.

In the cane sector, crop advances in leading producing countries such as Australia, Brazil, Cuba, South Africa and Thailand would be offset by a forecast fall in India, the world's largest single sugar producing nation, Man said.
While India posted a record outturn of 17.89 million tonnes raw value in 1995/96, this would now fall to 16.03 million.
With consumption placed at 13.7 million in white value terms, India would have an additional one million tonnes of sugar to either export or add to its already over-inflated stocks, Man said.
These were estimated to have stood at almost eight million tonnes at the end of the 1995/96 season.
Australia's tonnage of cane was forecast to rise to over 40 million tonnes for 1996/97 and final sugar production was pegged at a record 5.50 million tonnes after a previous 5.15 million.
Brazilian output was expected at 14.85 million tonnes, 566,000 tonnes up on 1995/96, with the centre-south growing area accounting for the bulk of the increase.

The Cuban harvest would produce 4.9 million tonnes of cane sugar in 1996/97, continuing its improvement from last year's 4.50 million, and Thailand would turn out 6.51 million tonnes versus a previous 6.35 million, the Man report said.
